provider: Blossom server fleet (24242.io, blossom.oslim.dev / Lotus, blossom.nostr.build)

free_tier.stated: 24242.io: free and unrestricted for now, 100MiB per file, files deleted if not accessed for 60 days. blossom.oslim.dev (Lotus): cost paid, retention permanent, max file size and storage per user not stated. blossom.nostr.build: free uploads up to 20 MiB per file, no limit on how many files and no expiry.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: The 24242.io policy states a 100MiB per-file cap. The Lotus README lists 100 MB per file and 8 GB per pubkey as defaults of the software, not as limits of the deployed blossom.oslim.dev server, whose page shows dashes for both.

retention.stated: 24242.io 100 MiB/file, deleted if not accessed for 60 days

egress.terms: unmetered / CDN-fronted. nostr.build advertises 'Global CDN delivery' on free uploads.

tooling: curl; hzrd149/blossom CLI; any Blossom client. BUD-04 `/mirror` lets one server pull a blob from another given a URL, so replication is a server-side call, not a client re-upload.
chaining: BUD-04 /mirror lets one Blossom server pull a blob from another server given a URL. 24242.io deletes files not accessed for 60 days; whether a HEAD request counts as an access is not stated.

limits.value: deleted if not accessed for 60 days

limits_note: 24242.io caps /list at the first 250 hits, so enumeration needs date ranges. Its per-file cap is 100MiB; nostr.build's free uploads are capped at 20 MiB. The deployed Lotus server publishes no file-size or per-user storage figure.
reliability_note: small volunteer hosts, several with unstated total capacity. 24242.io states 'Free and unrestricted... for now'. Prefer BUD-04 mirroring to two servers per chunk.

extras.unit_note: free_tier.unit is 'mixed' because the headline is denominated in MiB or KiB, which the schema enum does not carry; the verbatim free_tier.stated keeps the true unit. See the storage-dossier handover.
extras.verified_at_basis: re-checked against the first-party page on 2026-11-19 (a verify run); evidence rows dated by the seed pass, which ended 2026-10-21, keep that date as an upper bound
extras.quota_verbatim: 24242.io 100 MiB/file, deleted if not accessed for 60 days. blossom.oslim.dev (Lotus): 100 MB/file and 8 GB per pubkey, retention 'permanent', cost 'free'. blossom.nostr.build: 20 MiB/file free tier, 'no limit on how many files, and no expiry'.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap 100 MiB on most servers (20 MiB on nostr.build free). This is chunk-sized, not object-sized. 24242.io caps /list at the first 250 hits, so enumeration needs date ranges.
extras.egress_verbatim: unmetered / CDN-fronted. nostr.build advertises 'Global CDN delivery' on free uploads.
extras.chaining_verbatim: aggregate GB is the sum over the fleet x number of keypairs (oslim's 8 GB is per-pubkey, and pubkeys cost nothing). 24242.io's 60-day access-based retention is defeated by any periodic HEAD.
extras.tooling_verbatim: curl; hzrd149/blossom CLI; any Blossom client. BUD-04 `/mirror` lets one server pull a blob from another given a URL, so replication is a server-side call, not a client re-upload.
extras.agent_focus: Relay/P2P transport networks that could carry bulk data without a central provider. For each: is data ROUTED (a real path) or is it only SIGNALLING (relay coordinates, bytes go peer-to-peer)? Free bandwidth? Can it carry 1 TiB/day (= 12.7 MB/s = ~102 Mbit/s sustained)? Identity gate recorded as the primary ranking axis.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
